title: Hard Eligibility vs Optimization
summary: The Job Node Allocator enforces hard eligibility constraints before considering optimization metrics like cost or speed.
why: Security, legal, and access constraints are binary requirements; no amount of idle CPU or low cost can justify placing a job on an ineligible node.
invariants: Hard eligibility is evaluated before optimisation.
Security, legal, access, runtime/software, architecture, liveness, and mandatory resource constraints are never soft scores.
Hard constraints cannot be outweighed by idle CPU, free storage, cost, or speed.
